2023_297_troy_purchase_of_livernois_adja.paragraph: A revised real estate purchase agreement under which the Troy School District, a Michigan general powers school district at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, offers to buy 5856 Livernois (Sidwell Number 88-20-10-101-032) in the City of Troy, Oakland County, from Gary Abitheira and Brenda Abitheira of 985 Elmsford, Troy, Michigan 48083, for $733,333.34 payable in cash by wire transfer at closing. The parcel is one of three the district must close on simultaneously — the others being Sidwell Number 88-20-10-101-033 and 5874 Livernois (Sidwell Number 88-20-10-101-031) — to assemble a site for a new middle school, with the total combined purchase price for all three capped at $2,200,000.00. A $25,000.00 earnest money deposit is due to Chirco Title Agency within five business days of Board of Education approval, and the agreement becomes null and void if the Board does not approve it within fifteen business days.
2023_297_troy_purchase_of_livernois_adja.page:
**Parties and Property**
Purchaser: Troy School District, a Michigan general powers school district, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. Seller: Gary Abitheira and Brenda Abitheira, husband and wife, 985 Elmsford, Troy, Michigan 48083. Premises: Sidwell Number 88-20-10-101-032, commonly known as 5856 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, situated in the City of Troy, Oakland County, Michigan, depicted on Exhibit A and subject to Survey under Paragraph 5. The Premises includes all improvements, fixtures, appurtenances, access rights, tenements, hereditaments, oil, gas and mineral interests, water rights and other intangibles, subject only to existing building and use restrictions and easements of record.

**Price and Deposit**

| Item | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Purchase Price for 5856 Livernois | $733,333.34 |
| Earnest Money Deposit | $25,000.00 |
| Total combined price, all three properties | $2,200,000.00 |

The sale is a cash sale consummated by delivery of the Warranty Deed at Exhibit B conveying fee simple marketable title, payable by wire transfer at Closing. The deposit is due within five business days of the Board of Education's approval at a public meeting and is held in escrow by Chirco Title Agency, Attn: Michael Luberto, Esq., 26800 Harper Avenue, St Clair Shores, Michigan 48081, under the Escrow Agreement at Exhibit C.

**Title and Survey**
Seller must furnish a Commitment for Title Insurance within ten business days of the Date of this Agreement, issued by Chirco Title Agency and underwritten by Fidelity Title Insurance Company, in an amount not less than the Purchase Price. Purchaser may procure an ALTA survey at its own cost during the Inspection Period; the Survey legal description then governs, with a quit claim deed delivered at Closing if it differs from the Commitment. Seller has thirty days to cure written title or Survey objections or to instruct the Title Company to refund the deposit.

**Inspection and Environmental**
Purchaser has a sixty-day Inspection Period running from Board approval, during which it may conduct evaluations including a Phase I, a Phase II Environmental Site Assessment (ESA) and a Baseline Environmental Assessment (BEA). Confidential Disclosure Requirements bar Purchaser from disclosing findings to anyone other than Seller, its Board of Education, the Board's legal counsel and its real estate consultant Great Northern Consulting Group, and specifically bar disclosure to EGLE, MDEQ or any agency, until Closing. Purchaser must restore the Premises if it elects not to buy.

**Assemblage Contingency**
Seller acknowledges Purchaser is buying to construct a new middle school on the Premises and adjacent properties. The agreement is expressly contingent on simultaneous closing on Sidwell Number 88-20-10-101-033 and Sidwell Number 88-20-10-101-031 (5874 Livernois). Purchaser may provide an amendment at Closing reallocating the price among the three properties as the three Sellers mutually agree, so long as the combined total does not exceed $2,200,000.00.

**Costs, Closing and Approval**
Seller pays prior years' taxes, all special assessments assessed before Closing, and transfer taxes; Purchaser pays recording fees and title endorsements; closing costs are split equally. Current-year taxes prorate on a DUE DATE basis assuming summer and winter taxes are due July 1 and December 1. Closing occurs within thirty days of the later of satisfaction of conditions or delivery of the Commitment. Closing deliveries include a Closing Statement, FIRPTA certificates, Title Affidavits, the Warranty Deed and possession. The agreement is governed by Michigan law, is not effective until Board approval, and is null and void if the Board does not approve within fifteen business days of delivery of the Seller-executed agreement.

**Other Terms**
No broker or real estate agency is involved; Purchaser retained Great Northern Consulting Group and pays its fees separately. Purchaser will cooperate with a Section 1031 like-kind exchange at Seller's request at no cost to Purchaser. The Premises is sold as-is except for the Paragraph 12 representations. Exhibit D is the Purchase Agreement for Tallman Property. Documents were drafted by Dana L. Abrahams, Clark Hill PLC, 220 Park Street, Suite 200, Birmingham, MI 48009.
2023_297_troy_purchase_of_livernois_adja.verbose:
A revised Purchase Agreement between the Troy School District, a Michigan general powers school district whose address is 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (the Purchaser), and Gary Abitheira and Brenda Abitheira, husband and wife, whose address is 985 Elmsford, Troy, Michigan 48083 (collectively the Seller), for real property adjacent to Smith Middle School.

**Premises.** The property is situated in the City of Troy, Oakland County, Michigan, and is described as Sidwell Number 88-20-10-101-032, commonly known as 5856 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, as depicted on Exhibit A and subject to Survey as provided in Paragraph 5. The conveyance includes all improvements, fixtures and appurtenances now or hereafter on the Premises, subject only to existing building and use restrictions and easements of record. The term Premises includes all real property, buildings, improvements and structures, access rights, appurtenances, fixtures, tenements and hereditaments, together with any oil, gas and mineral interests, water rights and other intangibles owned or utilized by or for the benefit of Seller.

**Purchase price and form of sale.** The sale is to be consummated as a cash sale, with delivery of the form of Warranty Deed attached as Exhibit B conveying fee simple marketable title at Closing. The purchase price is Seven Hundred Thirty Three Thousand Three Hundred Thirty Three and 34/100 ($733,333.34) Dollars, payable by Purchaser at Closing via wire transfer, subject to Paragraph 11(C). Upon Seller's receipt of the Purchase Price at Closing, Seller delivers exclusive possession.

**Earnest money and escrow.** Within five business days of the Purchaser's Board of Education approving the transaction at a public Board of Education meeting, Purchaser deposits Twenty-Five Thousand and 00/100 ($25,000.00) Dollars as the Earnest Money Deposit, held in escrow by Chirco Title Agency, Attn: Michael Luberto, Esq., 26800 Harper Avenue, St Clair Shores, Michigan 48081 (the Title Company), pursuant to the Escrow Agreement attached as Exhibit C, and applied to the Purchase Price if the sale is consummated. Closing takes place at the Title Company's office, as otherwise agreed, or via an escrow closing.

**Title evidence.** Seller must furnish, within ten business days of the Date of this Agreement, a Commitment for Title Insurance with copies of all underlying title exception documents, issued by the Title Company and underwritten by Fidelity Title Insurance Company, in an amount not less than the Purchase Price. If Purchaser does not close for any reason other than its own default, Seller pays the Title Company for the cost of the Title Commitment. If Purchaser requires a without-exceptions Commitment, Purchaser procures an ALTA survey at its sole cost during the Inspection Period sufficient for the Title Company to issue an ALTA Owner's Policy without standard exceptions. Once accepted, the Survey legal description becomes the legal description of the Premises, and if it differs from the Commitment description, Seller delivers a quit claim deed at Closing in addition to the Warranty Deed. Seller pays for and orders the title policy consistent with the Commitment, updated to Closing; Purchaser pays for any endorsements it requests.

**Title objections.** On written objection, Seller has thirty days either to remedy the claimed defects or to instruct the Title Company to refund the Earnest Money Deposit in full termination. If Seller declines to cure, Purchaser's sole remedies are to waive the objections and continue, or to terminate and receive the deposit back, subject only to the Paragraph 11(A) restoration obligation. If Seller cures within the specified time, Purchaser completes the sale within thirty days after receipt of notification, revised Commitment or endorsement, or on the Paragraph 13 Closing date.

**Default.** On Purchaser default uncured within thirty days of written notice (or longer if diligent cure requires it and the parties agree on a period), Seller may enforce by specific performance or declare a breach and retain the Earnest Money Deposit as liquidated damages. On Seller default uncured within thirty days on the same terms, Purchaser may enforce by specific performance or declare a breach and receive an immediate refund of the entire deposit in full termination. From and after the date of the agreement, Seller shall not physically alter the Premises in any way.

**Taxes, assessments and closing costs.** Seller pays all special assessments assessed or constituting a lien as of Closing; Purchaser pays those arising after Closing. Seller pays all prior years' real and personal property taxes and all interest, rents and penalties on overdue taxes. Current-year real property taxes prorate on a DUE DATE basis for the municipality or taxing unit, assuming taxes are paid in advance and that summer and winter taxes are due and payable July 1 and December 1 respectively. Interest, rents, water and other utility bills prorate as of Closing. Seller pays all transfer taxes; Purchaser pays recording fees for the Warranty Deed and any Quit Claim Deed and the cost of any title endorsements it requests. Purchaser and Seller split Closing costs equally and have Chirco Title prepare the Closing documents.

**Inspection Period and environmental confidentiality.** Purchaser's obligations are contingent on its satisfaction following Survey, testing, analysis, inspection and evaluation (Purchaser's Evaluations). Purchaser has sixty days from the Board of Education's approval at a public meeting (the Inspection Period) to conduct them, which may include a Phase I, a Phase II Environmental Site Assessment (ESA) and a Baseline Environmental Assessment (BEA). Purchaser and its Representatives — employees, agents, representatives, engineers, inspectors and surveyors — have access at reasonable times, provided Purchaser first delivers certificates of insurance naming Seller as additional insured from any third party performing tests, surveys or environmental work. Purchaser must not allow liens; any inadvertent lien must be removed within five days of written notice, with reimbursement of Seller's reasonable attorney's fees. If Purchaser elects not to buy, it restores the Premises at its sole cost to a condition as good as before the Evaluations. Under the Confidential Disclosure Requirements, Purchaser may disclose only to Seller and, additionally, to its Board of Education, the Board's legal counsel and its real estate consultant Great Northern Consulting Group, and may not disclose any environmental studies or findings to any party or agency, including EGLE, MDEQ or any agency or person, without Seller's written permission, until Purchaser closes.

**Termination for dissatisfaction.** If Purchaser is dissatisfied with its Evaluations in its sole discretion, it may rescind and terminate without penalty by written notice on or before expiration of the Inspection Period, and Seller instructs the Title Company to return the deposit. Purchaser bears the cost of all Evaluations and provides copies to Seller within ten business days of receiving each final report. Seller must provide any tests, reports, analyses, leases or surveys in its possession within ten days of the Date of this Agreement. At any time during the Inspection Period, Purchaser may elect to purchase for the Purchase Price less the deposit by written notice.

**Three-parcel assemblage for a new middle school.** Seller acknowledges Purchaser is buying the Premises in order to construct a new middle school on the Premises as well as on other adjacent properties. To do so, Purchaser must also acquire Sidwell Number 88-20-10-101-033 and Sidwell Number 88-20-10-101-031 (commonly known as 5874 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098). The agreement is expressly contingent on Purchaser closing on the Premises and the additional two properties simultaneously; if it does not close on the other two, Purchaser may terminate immediately by written notice and the Title Company returns the deposit immediately. Purchaser has agreed to pay Two Million Two Hundred Thousand and 00/100 ($2,200,000.00) Dollars as a total combined purchase price for all three properties, and is willing to provide an amendment at Closing to Seller and the other two property owners reallocating the final purchase price among the three properties as mutually agreed by the three Sellers, so long as the combined total does not exceed $2,200,000.00. The Premises is otherwise sold as-is, with no representations except those in Paragraph 12.

**Seller representations and warranties.** Seller has complete, requisite and unrestricted power and authority to sell; Seller's interest transfers free and clear of all mortgages, land contract interests, leases, liens, security interests, pledges or charges; there are no judicial or administrative proceedings pending or threatened against the Premises; Seller is not party to any agreement, contract, land contract, lease or commitment in favor of any other person with an interest in or right to purchase or lease the Premises; Seller will complete the Purchaser's environmental consultant's standard owner's questionnaire in pursuance of the Phase I ESA; and each warranty, covenant and representation survives Closing.

**Closing deliveries.** Purchaser closes within thirty days of the later of satisfaction of the conditions or delivery of the Commitment. At Closing Seller delivers: (A) a Closing Statement executed by Seller and Purchaser; (B) FIRPTA certificates; (C) proof of Seller's authority; (D) Title Affidavits covering the Closing date showing title in Seller subject only to permitted exceptions; (E) a Warranty Deed; (F) a certificate that the representations and warranties remain true and correct; (G) possession of the Premises; (H) proof of payment of water/sewer bill and/or water and/or sewer escrow; and (I) other documents reasonably required by the Title Company.

**Effectiveness and board approval.** The Date of this Agreement is the date of acknowledgment of the signature of the last party to sign. The agreement is not effective until the Purchaser's Board of Education approves the transaction in a public meeting, even if signed by Purchaser beforehand, and it automatically becomes null and void if the Board fails to approve within fifteen business days of delivery of the Purchase Agreement to Purchaser already executed by Seller.

**Miscellaneous.** Dates falling on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday roll to the next business day. Waivers must be in writing and are not continuing. Michigan law governs. Seller acknowledges no broker or real estate agency was involved; Purchaser acknowledges it retained Great Northern Consulting Group and is responsible for its fees under a separate arrangement, with mutual indemnification for breach of that warranty. The agreement may be executed in counterparts, and facsimile and electronic signatures have the same force as originals. It constitutes the entire agreement, supersedes prior agreements, may be amended only in a signed writing, and binds heirs and successors. At Seller's request, Purchaser will cooperate with a like-kind exchange under Section 1031 of the Internal Revenue Code, including assignment of Seller's rights to a qualified intermediary at no cost to Purchaser, provided Purchaser need not incur additional cost, obligation or liability or accept title to other real property.

**Exhibits.** Exhibit A describes the Premises (Sidwell Number 88-20-10-101-032, 5856 Livernois). Exhibit B is the form Warranty Deed from Gary Abitheira and Brenda Abitheira as Grantor to Troy School District as Grantee, granting the right to make all legally permissible divisions under Section 108 of the Michigan Land Division Act, Act No. 288 of the Public Acts of 1967, as amended, and carrying the Michigan Right to Farm Act notice regarding proximity to farmland or a farm operation; it is to be notarized in Oakland County, Michigan, and was drafted by and is to be returned to Dana L. Abrahams, Clark Hill PLC, 220 Park Street, Suite 200, Birmingham, MI 48009. Exhibit C is the Escrow Agreement directed to Chirco Title Agency, 26800 Harper Avenue, St Clair Shores, Michigan 48081, covering the $25,000.00 check as Deposited Monies for the property at 5856 Livernois, releasing funds to Seller upon a satisfactorily executed closing statement or per joint written instructions, and providing that in a dispute the escrow agent may hold funds pending joint instructions or a final court order, with the parties reimbursing reasonable expenses including attorney fees in any litigation. Exhibit D is identified as the Purchase Agreement for Tallman Property. The document bears the reference 21968\472938\273147054.v4.

2024_298_2024_bod_elections_booklet_fina.paragraph: The Michigan Association of School Boards (MASB) 2024 Board of Directors election booklet, distributed to member boards including Troy, setting out membership rules, the seats up for election, voting procedures and candidate statements. Nine seats were on the ballot, but Regions 2, 3 and 4 and Group V went unopposed and Region 1 drew no nominations, leaving contested online balloting only in Regions 5, 6, 7 and 8. Ballots were emailed to each district's superintendent secretary on Jan. 26, 2024 and had to be cast and confirmed by 1 p.m. on Wednesday, March 6, 2024, with official results approved at the March 22, 2024 Board of Directors' meeting.
2024_298_2024_bod_elections_booklet_fina.page:
**Membership Structure (MASB Bylaws, Article IV, Section 2)**
The board of education of any public school district in Michigan may become an active member. Active members are divided into eight regions designated by intermediate school district boundaries. Region 1 covers Copper Country ISD, Delta-Schoolcraft ISD, Dickinson-Iron ISD, Eastern Upper Peninsula ISD, Gogebic-Ontonagon ISD, Marquette-Alger RESA and Menominee County ISD. Region 8 covers Macomb ISD, Oakland Schools and Wayne RESA. Members are also divided into seven groups by pupil membership: Group I all intermediate districts; Group II 0-1,400; Group III 1,401-2,500; Group IV 2,501-5,000; Group V 5,001-11,000; Group VI 11,001-40,000; Group VII more than 40,000.

**Board Composition and Limits**
The MASB Board of Directors comprises 24 members, including three at-large directors. Sixteen directors are elected from the eight regions, two per region, and one director per group is elected from Groups V, VI and VII. The MASB President nominates at-large directors subject to Board approval. Article VIII, Section 6 permits only one director from any one local or intermediate school district board. Article VIII, Section 8 provides that an unopposed nominee is declared elected without an election.

**Seats Up in 2024**
Nine seats, one each, three-year terms unless noted: Regions 1 (open seat), 2, 3 (one-year term), 4 (one-year term), 5, 6 (open seat), 7, 8, and Group V (one-year term).

| Seat | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Region 1 | Vacant; no nominations received |
| Region 2 | Dawn Kaiser, Iosco RESA, unopposed |
| Region 3 | Rick Dernberger, Zeeland Public Schools and Ottawa Area ISD, unopposed |
| Region 4 | John Tramontana, DeWitt Public Schools, unopposed |
| Group V | Stephen Hyer, Clarkston Community Schools, unopposed |
| Regions 5, 6, 7, 8 | Contested; online ballot |

**Voting Procedure**
Each district received one ballot, emailed to the superintendent secretary on record with MASB on Jan. 26, 2024; ballots cannot be forwarded. Completed ballots must be cast and confirmed by the superintendent secretary by 1 p.m. on Wednesday, March 6, 2024. Unofficial results are posted to the voicemail recording at 517.327.5915, generally after 2 p.m. on the deadline date, and emailed that afternoon; official results are approved at the March 22, 2024 Board of Directors' meeting. No local district or ISD funds may be used to campaign, including use of district email accounts; questions go to MASB Legal Counsel Brad Banasik, J.D., bbanasik@masb.org, 517.327.5929. Candidates receive a revocable license to an electronic file of member addresses limited to election communications. General questions: Cheryl Huffman, 517.327.5915, chuffman@masb.org.

**Candidates (incumbents noted)**
Region 5: Janice Holz, Huron Intermediate School District, Huron County (incumbent); Roshawnda Williams, Beecher Community School District, Genesee County. Region 6: Robert Becker, Barry Intermediate School District, Barry County; Pamela Dickinson, Comstock Public Schools, Kalamazoo County (incumbent); Elizabeth O'Dell, St. Joseph County ISD, St. Joseph County; Andrew Robinson, Berrien RESA, Berrien County. Region 7: Sharon Lee, Ypsilanti Community Schools, Washtenaw County; Michael McVey, Saline Area Schools, Washtenaw County; Jack Temsey, Eaton RESA, Eaton County; Mary Vincent, Monroe Public Schools, Monroe County; Dale Wingerd, Clinton Community Schools, Lenawee County (incumbent). Region 8: Melandie Hines, Wayne Westland Community Schools, Wayne County; Birgit McQuiston, Lake Orion Community Schools, Oakland County (incumbent); Evelyn Pridemore, Redford Union School District, Wayne County.

**Mission**
The mission of the Michigan Association of School Boards is to provide high-quality educational leadership services for all Michigan boards of education, and to advocate for an equitable and exceptional public education for all students.
2024_298_2024_bod_elections_booklet_fina.verbose:
The Michigan Association of School Boards (MASB) 2024 Board of Directors elections booklet, presenting the bylaws framework for membership, the schedule and rules for the 2024 election, and biographical and statement pages for each candidate.

**Membership regions.** Under MASB Bylaws Article IV, Section 2, the board of education of any public school district in Michigan may become an active member. Active members are divided into eight regions designated according to intermediate school district boundaries. Region 1: Copper Country ISD, Delta-Schoolcraft ISD, Dickinson-Iron ISD, Eastern Upper Peninsula ISD, Gogebic-Ontonagon ISD, Marquette-Alger RESA and Menominee County ISD. Region 2: Alpena-Montmorency-Alcona ESD, Charlevoix-Emmet ISD, Cheboygan-Otsego-Presque Isle ESD, COOR ISD, Iosco RESA, Manistee ISD, Northwest Education Services and Wexford-Missaukee ISD. Region 3: Ionia County ISD, Kent ISD, Mecosta-Osceola ISD, Montcalm Area ISD, Muskegon Area ISD, Newaygo County RESA, Ottawa Area ISD and West Shore ESD. Region 4: Bay-Arenac ISD, Clare-Gladwin RESD, Clinton County RESA, Gratiot-Isabella RESD, Midland County ESA, Saginaw ISD and Shiawassee RESD. Region 5: Genesee ISD, Huron ISD, Lapeer County ISD, Sanilac ISD, St. Clair County RESA and Tuscola ISD. Region 6: Allegan Area ESA, Barry ISD, Berrien RESA, Branch ISD, Calhoun ISD, Heritage Southwest ISD, Kalamazoo RESA, St. Joseph County ISD and Van Buren ISD. Region 7: Eaton RESA, Hillsdale County ISD, Ingham ISD, Jackson County ISD, Lenawee ISD, Livingston ESA, Monroe County ISD and Washtenaw ISD. Region 8: Macomb ISD, Oakland Schools and Wayne RESA.

**Membership groups.** Active members are also divided into seven groups based on pupil membership: Group I, all intermediate districts; Group II, school districts with a pupil membership of 0-1,400; Group III, 1,401-2,500; Group IV, 2,501-5,000; Group V, 5,001-11,000; Group VI, 11,001-40,000; and Group VII, more than 40,000.

**Board composition and election rules.** Nine seats on the MASB Board of Directors were up for election in 2024. The Board comprises 24 members, including three at-large directors. Sixteen directors are elected from the eight regions, two from each region, and one director per group is elected from Groups V, VI and VII. The MASB President nominates a member to serve as an at-large director, subject to Board approval. Article VIII, Section 6 of the MASB Bylaws permits only one director to be elected or appointed from any one local or intermediate school district board. Article VIII, Section 8 provides that if any nomination is unopposed, the Board of Directors declares the unopposed candidate elected without conducting an election for that group or region.

**Seats and uncontested outcomes.** The seats up were Regions 1 (open seat), 2, 3 (one-year term), 4 (one-year term), 5, 6 (open seat), 7, 8 and Group V (one-year term), one seat each and three-year terms unless otherwise noted. Region 1 had a vacant seat as no nominations were received. Region 2 continues to be represented by Dawn Kaiser, Iosco RESA (unopposed, no ballots sent). Region 3 continues with Rick Dernberger, Zeeland Public Schools and Ottawa Area Intermediate School District (unopposed). Region 4 continues with John Tramontana, DeWitt Public Schools (unopposed). Group V continues with Stephen Hyer, Clarkston Community Schools (unopposed). Voting in Regions 5, 6, 7 and 8 took place via online ballot.

**Voting procedures.** Each district received one ballot, emailed to the superintendent secretary on record with MASB on Jan. 26, 2024; ballots could not be forwarded. Boards conveyed their choice to the superintendent secretary, and completed ballots had to be cast and confirmed by 1 p.m. on Wednesday, March 6, 2024. Unofficial results were made available on the voicemail recording at 517.327.5915, generally after 2 p.m. on the deadline date, and emailed that afternoon; official results were to be approved at the March 22, 2024 Board of Directors' meeting, which newly elected directors should plan to attend. No local district or ISD funds could be used to campaign, a rule that prohibits candidates from using school district email accounts to message other board members, requiring a personal account instead; questions about what constitutes an expenditure of district funds go to MASB Legal Counsel Brad Banasik, J.D., at bbanasik@masb.org or 517.327.5929. An electronic file of physical and email addresses for the voting group or region was made available to each candidate under a revocable license limited to contacting school board members about the election. General questions were directed to Cheryl Huffman at 517.327.5915 or chuffman@masb.org.

**Region 5 candidates.** Janice Holz, incumbent, Huron Intermediate School District, Huron County: 32 years on that board and 25 years on the Bad Axe Public Schools board, having held President, Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer on both; MASB certifications include Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction, Master Boardmember Award, Master Diamond Award, Master Platinum Award, President's Award of Recognition, Advocacy Specialty and Data Specialty. She cites experience as an ISD board member, current MASB Director and SET SEG Director, and names mental health, more school counselors, suicide prevention, social emotional support, artificial intelligence, student achievement, truancy, diversity, equity and inclusion, and administrative and teacher shortages as issues. Roshawnda Williams, Beecher Community School District, Genesee County: a trustee of six years who has lived in the Beecher School District for 15 years, has served as Treasurer, and holds the Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit and Award of Distinction. Her motto is that passion and positivity can make the impossible happen; contact 810.936.1615, roshawnda.williams63@gmail.com.

**Region 6 candidates.** Robert Becker, Barry Intermediate School District, Barry County: six years on the board, having served as President and Vice President, holding the Certified Boardmember Award and Award of Merit. A former classroom teacher, central office administrator for operations and school superintendent, he volunteers on the boards of Court Appointed Special Advocates, Barry County Community Mental Health Authority, Barry Intermediate School District and the Family Support Center of Barry County, and has served on the MASB Government Relations Committee. Pamela Dickinson, incumbent, Comstock Public Schools, Kalamazoo County: 10 years listed for time served, with offices of President, Vice President and Treasurer; certifications include Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction, Master Boardmember Award, Master Diamond Award, Advocacy Specialty and Data Specialty. She states she has served as Comstock board President for the last five years and as a board member for nine years, and currently serves as a Member At-Large on the MASB Board of Directors. Elizabeth O'Dell, St. Joseph County ISD, St. Joseph County: 26 years on the board, with offices of President, Vice President and Treasurer; certifications include Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction, Master Boardmember Award and Master Diamond Award, and she notes obtaining the level 5, Master Diamond award. She holds a bachelor's degree from Ball State University and a graduate degree from Western Michigan University, is a retired CEO of St. Joseph County Community Mental Health, and volunteers with Red Cross Disaster Relief, local substitute teaching and Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated. Andrew Robinson, Berrien RESA, Berrien County: three years on the board, serving as Treasurer; he is near completion of a Doctor of Education in Organizational Leadership and Development and works with Mosaic CCDA, a workforce and community development agency in Benton Harbor, and Emerge Innovation Hub, an entrepreneurial support organization in Southwest Michigan.

**Region 7 candidates.** Sharon Lee, Ypsilanti Community Schools, Washtenaw County: nine years of service, with offices of President, Vice President and Secretary and currently holding the position of Vice President; certifications include Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction, Master Boardmember Award, Master Diamond Award, Advocacy Specialty and Data Specialty. She volunteers at Joyful Treats Community Development Corp., led by Ms. Khadija Wallace, distributing food in the Ypsilanti community, and highlights staff training through A.L.I.C.E., Threat Assessment and Mental Health First Aid, and youth homelessness as a pressing issue. Michael McVey, Saline Area Schools, Washtenaw County: seven years on the board, with offices of President, Vice President and Secretary; certifications include Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction, Master Boardmember Award, Master Diamond Award, Master Platinum Award, President's Award of Recognition and Advocacy Specialty. He describes over 40 years serving students and schools, beginning as an ELA and Special Education teacher, teaching ESL for a year in Japan, authoring Meeting the Internet Challenge, training teachers at The University of Arizona, earning a doctorate in Education, and becoming a professor of Teacher Education at Eastern Michigan University; he was Washtenaw Association of School Boards president, expects to receive the President's Award in the spring, and serves on the Governmental Relations Committee. Jack Temsey, Eaton RESA, Eaton County: seven years on the Eaton RESA board and eight years on the Potterville Public Schools Board of Education; offices include President, Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer; certifications include Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction, Master Boardmember Award, Master Diamond Award, Master Platinum Award, Advocacy Specialty and Data Specialty. At Potterville he served on the Policy, Community Relations and Technology Committees; at Eaton RESA on Building and Grounds and Finance and Audit, and he is currently serving again as President. For MASB he has served on the Curriculum and Instruction Committee and the Government Relations Committee, including as its Vice Chairman, and concluded a term as Vice Chairman of the Resolutions and Bylaws committee. He advocates adequate and equitable funding for all districts. Mary Vincent, Monroe Public Schools, Monroe County: two years on the board, serving as Secretary; certifications include Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Data Specialty and Advocacy Specialty. She holds a bachelor's degree in K-12 music education and a master's in K-12 administration and educational leadership, taught public school music in southeast Michigan for 16 years across Y5-12 in general music, band, entrepreneurship and technology, is entering her second year as board secretary, and since May 2023 has earned an Award of Merit, Data Specialty and Advocacy Specialty while serving on the MASB Resolutions and Bylaws Committee. Dale Wingerd, incumbent, Clinton Community Schools, Lenawee County: 17 years on that board and two years on Lenawee ISD; offices of President and Secretary; certifications include Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction, Master Boardmember Award, Master Diamond Award, Master Platinum Award and President's Award of Recognition. He notes service on several committees through two terms with MASB.

**Region 8 candidates.** Melandie Hines, Wayne Westland Community Schools, Wayne County: 10 years on the board, with offices of Vice President and Secretary; certifications include Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction and Master Boardmember Award. She states that in 2018 she helped pass a $150 million bond across six communities, listing Wayne, Westland, Dearborn Heights, Romulus and Inkster, and recently passed a $24.5 million bond for the Westwood Community Schools, and is working on a skilled trades program with the Taylor Career Technical Center. Birgit McQuiston, incumbent, Lake Orion Community Schools, Oakland County: 12 years listed for time served, with offices of President, Vice President and Secretary; certifications include Certified Boardmember Award, Award of Merit, Award of Distinction, Master Boardmember Award, Master Diamond Award, Master Platinum Award, President's Award of Recognition, Advocacy Specialty and Data Specialty. She serves on the Lake Orion Board of Education, the Oakland County School Boards Association Board of Directors and the MASB Board of Directors, where in three years she has served on the Executive, Finance and Policy Committees, currently chairs the Government Relations Committee, and was appointed by the State Board of Education as the MASB representative to a three-year term on the Special Education Advisory Committee, which advises the State Board and the Michigan Department of Education. Evelyn Pridemore, Redford Union School District, Wayne County: 11 years listed for time served, with offices of President, Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer. She states she has served her local district for almost 12 years, has been through deficit, declining enrollment and the changes COVID brought, currently serves as President, was recently appointed to the leadership team for WCASB, and has guided her district through two superintendent searches and a multi-million-dollar bond initiative while serving on policy, finance, curriculum and facilities committees. She mentions a husband of 36 years, three sons, two daughters-in-law and three grandchildren.

**Mission statement.** The mission of the Michigan Association of School Boards is to provide high-quality educational leadership services for all Michigan boards of education, and to advocate for an equitable and exceptional public education for all students.

2025_299_nov_2024_financial_statement.paragraph: Unaudited Troy School District statements of revenues and expenditures for the period July 1, 2024 through November 30, 2024, covering the General Fund, Consolidated Debt Service Funds, four special revenue funds, two capital projects funds and the Sinking Fund. General Fund revenues totaled $54,092,233 against expenditures of $56,900,642, leaving revenues under expenditures of $(2,808,409) for the five months, compared with an approved budget of $192,509,567 in revenues and $194,936,368 in expenditures. The 2023 Capital Projects Fund (423) recorded the largest activity outside the General Fund, with $20,014,866 in expenditures against $4,057,523 in revenues.

2025_299_nov_2024_financial_statement.verbose:
Unaudited statements of revenues and expenditures for the Troy School District covering the Period July 1, 2024 - November 30, 2024, presented fund by fund with an approved budget column and an actual column. The General Fund page is dated 12/17/24; the Consolidated Debt Service, Food Service, Troy Career Center, Community Service, Troy Preschool, 2023 Capital Projects and Sinking Fund pages carry the budget date 6/20/24, and the 2019 Capital Projects page shows 6/20/2024.

**General Fund revenues.** Local Sources were budgeted at 47,240,605 with actual receipts of 23,099,184. State Sources were budgeted at 127,322,515 with actual of 27,932,835. Federal Sources were budgeted at 4,108,082 with actual of 205,100. Interdistrict Sources were budgeted at 13,838,365 with actual of 2,855,114. Total Revenues were budgeted at $192,509,567 with actual of $54,092,233.

**General Fund instruction.** Basic Programs were budgeted at 91,558,112 with actual expenditures of 24,737,167. Added Needs were budgeted at 30,085,945 with actual of 8,602,142. Adult Education was budgeted at 1,083,330 with actual of 259,612. Total Instruction was budgeted at 122,727,387 with actual of 33,598,921.

**General Fund support services.** Pupil support was budgeted at 16,303,720 with actual of 4,240,871. Instructional Staff was budgeted at 12,964,602 with actual of 3,798,842. General Administration was budgeted at 2,505,398 with actual of 882,907. School Administration was budgeted at 10,176,228 with actual of 3,321,969. Business Services was budgeted at 2,402,724 with actual of 671,601. Operations was budgeted at 15,306,065 with actual of 5,874,319. Pupil Transportation was budgeted at 5,141,953 with actual of 1,348,109. Central Services was budgeted at 3,794,770 with actual of 1,940,658. Support Services (Athletics and Other) was budgeted at 2,652,220 with actual of 1,026,176. Total Support Services was budgeted at 71,247,680 with actual of 23,105,453.

**General Fund other expenditures and result.** Community Services was budgeted at 315,004 with actual of 80,652. Debt Service was budgeted at 478,500 with actual of 115,617. Outgoing Transfers were budgeted at 167,797 with no actual recorded. Total Expenditures were budgeted at $194,936,368 with actual of $56,900,642. Revenues Over (Under) Expenditures were budgeted at $(2,426,801) with actual of $(2,808,409).

**Consolidated Debt Service Funds.** Local Sources were budgeted at 31,650,700 with actual of 15,864,841, and State Sources at 279,800 with actual of 360,169, for Total Revenues budgeted at $31,930,500 and actual of $16,225,010. On the expenditure side, Principal was budgeted at 21,415,000 with no actual recorded for the period; Interest was budgeted at 10,292,530 with actual of 5,146,265; and Other Transactions were budgeted at 2,000 with actual of 650. Total Expenditures were budgeted at $31,709,530 with actual of $5,146,915. Revenues Over (Under) Expenditures were budgeted at $220,970 with actual of $11,078,095, reflecting that the tax levy had been collected while no principal payment had yet come due.

**Special Revenue Fund - Food Service Fund (520).** Local Sources were budgeted at 443,500 with actual of 85,534; State Sources at 4,500,000 with actual of 1,156,961; Federal Sources at 1,750,000 with actual of 637,669; and Interdistrict Sources with no budget and actual of 700. Total Revenues were budgeted at $6,693,500 with actual of $1,880,864. Expenditures: Salaries budgeted at 85,807 with actual of 35,034; Employee Benefits at 7,500 with actual of 2,680; Purchased Services at 2,675,000 with actual of 979,317; Supplies and Materials at 3,200,000 with actual of 1,026,300; Capital Outlay at 300,000 with actual of 209,110; Other at 93,000 with actual of 6,216; and Transfers Out at 37,000 with no actual. Total Expenditures were budgeted at $6,398,307 with actual of $2,258,657. Revenues Over (Under) Expenditures were budgeted at $295,193 with actual of $(377,793), meaning the fund ran an operating deficit for the period.

**Special Revenue Fund - Troy Career Center Fund (529).** State Sources show no budget and no actual. Federal Sources were budgeted at 2,623,839 with actual of 1,317,675. Total Revenues were budgeted at $2,623,839 with actual of $1,317,675. Expenditures: Salaries budgeted at 1,038,645 with actual of 441,434; Employee Benefits at 588,694 with actual of 262,420; Purchased Services at 731,500 with actual of 456,536; Supplies and Materials at 10,000 with actual of 5,188; Capital Outlay at 5,000 with actual of 7,210; Other at 106,500 with actual of 107,885; and Debt Service at 143,500 with actual of 37,002. Total Expenditures were budgeted at $2,623,839 with actual of $1,317,675, so Revenues Over (Under) Expenditures were nil in both the budget and actual columns, consistent with a fully grant-reimbursed operation. Capital Outlay and Other had each already exceeded their full-year budget lines.

**Special Revenue Fund - Community Service Fund (530).** Local Sources were budgeted at 2,050,000 with actual of 813,818, and that was the only revenue line, giving Total Revenues budgeted at $2,050,000 and actual of $813,818. Expenditures: Salaries budgeted at 752,356 with actual of 259,013; Employee Benefits at 415,529 with actual of 125,513; Purchased Services at 825,000 with actual of 352,051; Supplies and Materials at 35,000 with actual of 13,523; Capital Outlay at 20,000 with no actual; and Other with no budget and no actual. Total Expenditures were budgeted at $2,047,885 with actual of $750,100. Revenues Over (Under) Expenditures were budgeted at $2,115 with actual of $63,718.

**Special Revenue Fund - Troy Preschool Fund (531).** Local Sources were budgeted at 2,275,000 with actual of 807,322, and State Sources at 1,921,657 with actual of 631,772, giving Total Revenues budgeted at $4,196,657 and actual of $1,439,094. Expenditures: Salaries budgeted at 1,390,577 with actual of 522,793; Employee Benefits at 765,190 with actual of 271,496; Purchased Services at 951,337 with actual of 289,042; Supplies and Materials at 230,999 with actual of 67,596; Capital Outlay at 92,336 with actual of 2,854; Other at 37,479 with actual of 1,146; and Debt Service at 602,590 with actual of 100,833. Total Expenditures were budgeted at $4,070,508 with actual of $1,255,759. Revenues Over (Under) Expenditures were budgeted at $126,149 with actual of $183,335.

**2019 Capital Projects Fund (419).** Local Sources were budgeted at 60,000 with actual of 25,335. Capital Outlay was budgeted at 1,000,000 with actual of 30,845, and Support Services - Central shows no budget and no actual. Total Revenue was budgeted at $60,000 with actual of $25,335; Total Expenditures budgeted at $1,000,000 with actual of $30,845; and Revenues Over (Under) Expenditures budgeted at $(940,000) with actual of $(5,510). Spending in this older bond fund had nearly wound down.

**2023 Capital Projects Fund (423).** Local Sources were budgeted at 6,000,000 with actual of 4,057,523. Expenditures: Purchased Services budgeted at 2,258,369 with actual of 134,769; Capital Outlay budgeted at 84,151,206 with actual of 19,785,995; and Outgoing Transfers budgeted at 1,190,425 with actual of 94,103. Total Revenue was budgeted at $6,000,000 with actual of $4,057,523; Total Expenditures budgeted at $87,600,000 with actual of $20,014,866; and Revenues Over (Under) Expenditures budgeted at $(81,600,000) with actual of $(15,957,343). This is by far the largest construction program reported, financed from bond proceeds rather than current-period revenue, so the negative result is expected.

**Sinking Fund (498).** For the same period, Local Sources were budgeted at 5,115,000 with actual of 2,488,043, and Capital Outlay was budgeted at 5,000,000 with actual of 2,674,010. Total Revenue was budgeted at $5,115,000 with actual of $2,488,043; Total Expenditures budgeted at $5,000,000 with actual of $2,674,010; and Revenues Over (Under) Expenditures budgeted at $115,000 with actual of $(185,967).

**Overall.** Across the district's funds for the first five months of fiscal year 2024-25, the General Fund, Food Service Fund, 2019 Capital Projects Fund, 2023 Capital Projects Fund and Sinking Fund each reported expenditures exceeding revenues, while the Consolidated Debt Service Funds, Community Service Fund and Troy Preschool Fund reported revenues exceeding expenditures and the Troy Career Center Fund reported an exact match. The statements are labeled unaudited throughout.
